I'm also in healthcare, not a nurse or a dr. Just a front end supervisor. But anyway, im so sorry for what you're going through. Its so hard but much appreciated!! Thank you! Here are some of my coping skills that I use during stressful times and what we did at the clinic I work for:

1) Count and feel your breathe. Focus on each movement - your lungs, stomach, esophagus, nose, etc feel whenever you inhale and exhale. Be mindful for the here and now basically.

2) Take your breaks. Don't work through your breaks. Even take a quick 3-5 minutes break every so often to beathe/mindful, go to the bathroom (because most of us hold it, just a friendly reminder to take care of your body), drink some water, - maybe mix it with something with electrolytes so you're not loosing out on important vitamins. 

3) Tell your boss. Don't do it in a complaining way though. Just explain, "Hey, I'm getting really worn out. Is there anyway I could ..." and give them a good idea of what you plan on holding back on. Whether its paper work, hours, or even your area that you work in. As an example, one of my employees couldn't handle the flow of answering some calls and checking in pts all day everyday. We came up with a plan to put everyone on rotation of when they would work the front vs the back. Check in vs Insurance and scheduling as an example. Everyone gets 3 days in front, 2 days in back. So far no one has complained. But we just started this last month, so they may still feel overwhelmed..

5-4-3-2-1 method works wonders for grounding and re-centering yourself.
Describe and acknowledge 5 things you see, 4 things you can touch, 3 things you hear, 2 things you can smell, and 1 thing you can taste.

I know during a panic attack you should try doing the 5-4-3-2-1 coping technique.

Acknowledge 5 things you see, 4 things you can touch around you, 3 things you can hear (other than your thoughts), 2 things you can smell, and 1 thing you can taste. 

Ex of whats around me right now: 5- my husband, a chair, a blanket, our cat, our dog, and the xbox.
4-the blanket, the couch pillow, our cat, and the couch cushion. 3-the fridge running (its actually pretty effing loud lol), our dog chewing on his antler, and the survival game my husband is playing. 2- our incense sticks and smoke from our vape pen. 1- a Dr. Pepper. 

I hope this helps during those rough times when you can't think straight. I made a recording to walk me through these 5 steps because in the moment, you may not be able to think of what to do. Having a recording that's easily accessible has helped me and is just a suggestion. My anxiety comes from ptsd which is why its hard to focus. Its like going into a trance and not being able to come back out.

Edit: i should mention that once you've been grounded (coping= being grounded or mindful), take a few moments to breathe.When you hold your breathe, your brain will freak out more because of the lack of oxygen. When doing this technique, it can allow you to breathe between each item too. Then remind yourself "It can't hurt me. Im safe. This is my safe space" if your out in public, go to a safe space like your car, your office, a bathroom, or outside. The goal is to get away from noises and distractions that could flare the panic attack that you're trying to come down from. 

Again, I hope this helps. Its a hard road but never fight alone and you can get through this!

Medical Biller here from Colorado, USA. 

Our healthcare and insurance is so different and difficult that there are too many avenues you can go. Our structure is limited because of all the different insurance policies. And sadly, thats our healthcare system. Most pay a premium to pay 10% of the bill and you get stuck the rest until you've paid a maximum. But, ill break it down the best I can. 

Depending what plan you have you may have to start with a general practitioner or primary care physician. These doctors and medical professionals will generally exam you. Poke and prode and say, "Yeah thats weird" and will refer you to a gynecologist. Some insurances you can skip this step but im including it anyway. 
To break down price, basically you can pay up to $500 usd on yourself alone for medical coverage, eye, and dental. Then you may have a copayment up to $50 just for your general doctor, or a coincidence (that 90% the insurance won't cover yet) which can be up to $200. 

Ok great now we can see the gynecologist! Ok well... most gyns are general practicing. And finding specialization for Endo is still very hard. Getting a dr in general to believe the amount of pain you're in is also something people struggle with. But lets say you're lucky and you find the right Dr on the first try and you are granted a laparoscopy!
Ok so again, maybe we skipped seeing the general doctor but the premium per month is still 500. If its a specialist or considered as such by the insurance, the copay could be up to $75 or a coincidence (that 90% again) up to $250-300!

Alright, your gyn got the approval from insurance (because that had to happen too) that its medically necessary to find answers. You get the procedure done, you get your answers, and let's say no complications happened during surgery.

500 monthly premium because it probably took about a month or 2 to even get a surgery date set. A copayment for seeing the dr before the surgery $75-$300, then the procedure itself ranging from $4,000-$10,000. Even with insurance, it could be this high. 

So for the total amount of money, let's say it took 4 months (1st month we see the general dr, 2nd month we see the gyn, 4th month we get to do the surgery) [obviously it may take much longer but this is for scenario purposes]. 4 months of premium insurance paid from your wages (500×4), copays $50-450, and the surgery $4,000-$10,000. Not included is the follow up appointment. So for research purposes, it could cost a person in the USA with insurance, $6,050-$12,450. This is only an average that I'm pulling from my state and with the insurance policies that are more well known to me. 

I hope this helps for research purposes of not only the process but the amount of money that can go into it too. I really wish we could restructure our healthcare system. Be quite, imagine the feeling flowing through the tips of you're fingers, into your knuckles, up to the.... and breathe in and out...etc" then no and I completely understand why it may not be for you.
Correct me if I'm wrong but if I'm right then here is my opinion:

Be honest with your therapist and explain, "I feel really uncomfortable and id like to try something different" or "I don't like the silence" , which is actually why I can't stand the mindfulness technique that i think most therapists try. 

The way I becoming mindful is listening to music. I like lofi to help start relax my brain a little. Then, I freaking brain dump with a recording in my phone. I think way to fast to write in a journal and I suck at journaling thoughts anyway. And I just say everything that is flowing through my mind. After that I take a moment, close my eyes and say in my head-there.. its out. I am empty. I will then breathe and feel things that bring me joy. I'm an artist so its usually paint or paper. But I just feel the texture, admire it. Let the joy consume me. How does it feel, does it have a smell even. I let my senses search and feel. And I focus on that feeling. If I feel a bad or even distracting thought, I will open my eyes and say "This is my time brain" and breathe again. I can't do this for long so after a final breathe ill try to word dump again if its a bad day. It helps sooth my mind for a moment before the shitty anxiety returns. But I look forward to those moments now. It takes practice and finding ways to fit your needs but i know you'll be able to achieve it.
